_comment: Exact expected values for a handful of items. These pin the parts of the pipeline where a subtle regression would otherwise pass every count-based check.

item_0425._why: Pins the %% rule. The source string is '...movement speed by %ability_self_movespeed_pct%%%', which must render as one percent sign, not two and not a swallowed digit.
item_0425.descPlain_en: Active: ClumsyWhen activated, reduces your own movement speed by 25%, but grants 50% of maximum attack damage and 30% max health for 10 seconds.

item_0100._why: Pins CDN icon resolution and recipe parsing, including the implicit count of 1 on an ingredient written without a ':n' suffix.

item_G001._why: Pins gem_value pair parsing and lore extraction.

item_s_0305._why: Fate stone: pins the 'item_s_' id shape surviving lowercased token lookup.

item_P203._why: Pins multi-ingredient recipes with explicit counts.

item_M001._why: Base material, the most-referenced ingredient in the crafting graph.

item_tango._why: The one vanilla Dota item in the table. Its ItemQuality is the string 'consumable' rather than a number, and it is not in the game — it must be excluded from the playable index without crashing the normalizer.

item_0200._why: Dismantle: quality-6 treasure. Yields Legendary Essence outright plus Mythic at 25% — the only rule with two outputs of different certainty.

item_0102._why: Dismantle: quality-5 treasure at level 1, the branch where the addon splits 50/50 between Legendary and plain Equipment Essence.

item_0099._why: Dismantle: quality-5 treasure above level 1, which drops the 50/50 split for a guaranteed Legendary Essence.

item_0157._why: Dismantle: quality-5 equipment that is not a treasure — pins the treasure test itself, since quality and level alone would not separate it from item_0099.

graph._why: Every ingredient of this recipe must carry a reverse usedBy link.

abilities._comment: Hero abilities come from a different source than items — a CSV translation table rather than the KeyValues locale files — and their icons resolve through three paths. These pin all of it.

axe_003._why: Pins the CSV locale join end to end: name, substituted description and per-value labels, plus a stock ability icon fetched by plain name.
axe_003.descPlain_en: When attacked, has a 25% chance to trigger Counter Helix, dealing physical damage equal to 30% of your max health and max shield to enemy units within a 275 radius.

axe_004._why: The addon ships its own art for this one, so it must come out of resource/flash3/images/spellicons rather than the CDN.

drow_004._why: A pathed texture name. The CDN only answers to the basename, so path stripping must happen before the fetch.

lina_009._why: Names a cosmetic Phoenix texture that the CDN does not carry and whose stock counterpart is a different spell, so it is pinned to the hand-supplied override rather than an alias.

ak_hero_heal._why: The shared f heal: no profession gates it, every hero equips it, and it is the only candidate for its key — so it is attached to all five heroes and preselected. Its texture is published nowhere, so this also pins the hand-supplied override in assets/ability-icons.

heroes._comment: Roster positions are baked into every shared guide, and the unfinished-ability filter decides what a hero may be built around.

npc_dota_hero_axe._why: Pins the frozen roster index and the grouping of abilities by the key they bind to — several candidates per key is the whole build decision. axe_009 is absent on purpose: no hero AbilityN or talent node grants it.

npc_dota_hero_lina._why: Pins two rules at once: the key a season ruleset assigns (Burning Thunder, lina_014, has no AbilitySlot in the base payload and must still land in q), and the obtainability filter (lina_002, lina_006, lina_007 and lina_010 have finished rows but no hero AbilityN or talent node grants them, so they must not be offered).

npc_dota_hero_crystal_maiden._why: Every one of her own abilities is still a 'To be filled.' placeholder upstream, so she must be rostered offering nothing but the shared heal, rather than five spells that do not exist.
